recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中央靠近脂肪空泡處有兩顆並排、均質亮粉紅色的圓形球體，就是細胞質內免疫球蛋白堆積形成的 Russell bodies；周圍是細胞密度高的造血組織夾雜多顆核偏心的漿細胞。
features: Two adjacent round, homogeneous, glassy eosinophilic globules (Russell bodies) near an adipocyte
Hypercellular marrow with mixed hematopoietic elements including erythroid precursors with dense round nuclei and maturing granulocytes
Scattered cells with eccentric nuclei and amphophilic cytoplasm consistent with plasma cells
Occasional larger cells with vesicular nuclei; no sheets of atypical plasma cells clearly identifiable
Image resolution is moderate and limits cytologic detail
describe_en: H&E-stained bone marrow biopsy section shows a hypercellular marrow with trilineage hematopoietic elements between adipocytes. Near the center, two adjacent round, homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic intracytoplasmic globules are present, consistent with Russell bodies. Scattered plasma cells with eccentric nuclei are identified, but sheets of plasma cells are not clearly evident and resolution limits cytologic detail. Russell bodies reflect immunoglobulin accumulation in distended endoplasmic reticulum and are seen in both reactive and neoplastic plasma cell proliferations; CD138 and kappa/lambda staining are needed to assess plasma cell burden and clonality.

ddx.vs: Erythrocytes are smaller, biconcave and paler centrally, whereas Russell bodies are larger, spherical, uniformly dense and PAS-positive.
Dutcher bodies overlie or invaginate the nucleus as apparent intranuclear inclusions, whereas these globules are separate from the nucleus in the cytoplasm.
Eosinophils have many small coarse orange granules and bilobed nuclei rather than one or two large smooth homogeneous globules.
